question: What evidence is there about how clients under 40 choose a financial advisor?

adjacent.text: On the 3Q25 earnings call (published 2025-10-16), Schwab CEO Rick Wurster said "Their top online resource is YouTube," and that Schwab is the number one financial services firm on YouTube by followers. He also said one-third of retail households who created a financial plan within the last two years are under the age of 40, and that younger traders are turning to Schwab because of its platforms, tools, education, coaching, expertise and service.
adjacent.differs_because: This is management's description of younger Schwab clients' engagement and why younger traders come to Schwab. It is not a study of how under-40 clients select a financial advisor, and the chunk does not say whom "Their" refers to.

adjacent.text: UBS research on the next generation (published 2026-04-22, 'What does the next generation look for in a wealth manager?') reports that when choosing a wealth manager, experience and expertise sit at the top of the next generation's wish list (79%). More than half (56%) want advisors who can build trusted relationships across generations, and 41% want advisors who fully understand the next generation's needs.
adjacent.differs_because: The survey covers the 'next generation' (heirs of wealthy families, including entrepreneurs) choosing a wealth manager. The chunk does not define it as clients under 40, so it is not an under-40 population.

adjacent.text: A CFP Board-type consumer survey (published 2025-06-06) found Americans are most confident in financial information from a qualified, competent financial advisor. It also found that those aged 25-45 are more trusting than Americans aged 46-64 of information from generative AI tools (44% vs. 26%) and social media (44% vs. 24%).
adjacent.differs_because: This is about trust in financial information sources, including online ones, for ages 25-45. It does not address how people choose an advisor, and the age band is 25-45, not under 40.

gaps.what: Direct evidence on how clients under 40 choose a financial advisor (selection criteria, referral or discovery channels, decision drivers) is not found in the evidence provided. The closest items are a Schwab management comment on younger clients, UBS next-generation survey data and a consumer trust survey (see adjacent).
gaps.suggested_source: Age-segmented investor survey on advisor selection (e.g., Cerulli, J.D. Power, Northwestern Mutual, or a CFP Board study with an under-40 cut), or firm client-acquisition research broken out by age.
